what_happened: Job 20261105-180330-tb41 ("Take a build slot for each producer cargo command", code) failed in planning, before any code was written. After round 5 of 5 the critic still said the plan needed revising. It confirmed most of the plan's claims against the code: the slot queue functions, the producer class, the hook dispatch, the policy functions, the invocation record, and that only the producer passes Side::Produce. It found one major gap: the policy lets the producer put global flags before the subcommand (`cargo -q build`, `cargo --locked test`), and the plan's own policy rule requires the wrapper for those forms. But the plan never says how the wrapper finds the subcommand. `cargo_subcommand` is a private function in policy.rs, and the criterion 1 tests use only bare `cargo build/test/clippy/check`. A wrapper that looked at only its first argument would run those forms with no slot, and no test would catch it. Four minor findings: the hook checks its own PATH, not the Bash tool's; the "not failed" test cannot fail without the feature; the peak is sampled only when a producer command wins a slot; and one nit on line references. Six more minor findings said files such as invocation.rs, reading.rs, pr_check.rs, reconcile.rs, landing_tests.rs and docs/records.md are not among the reading's deliverables. The critic noted that decision 17 already explains these. No acceptance criteria were reported unmet and no checks failed. Nothing was delivered.
cause: Planning checks that the seams a plan names exist. It does not make the plan walk the real input forms that existing code accepts, here the global-flag grammar in CARGO_GLOBAL_FLAGS, and share one parser between the rule and the new wrapper. The plan's tests used only the simplest command shapes, so its own demonstrations could not expose the gap. The plan wrote its policy rule from the accepted forms but left the wrapper's subcommand lookup unspecified. The critic ran five rounds and kept raising small findings, including six scope notes that decision 17 had already answered. That made it hard to settle the one real gap. Planning has fixed rounds, keeps no partial plan and has no repair step, so a code-answerable gap left after the last round loses all planning spend.
prevention: When a plan adds a wrapper, rule or parser for commands that an existing rule already accepts in several forms, the planner should have to do four things in the plan. First, list the real accepted forms from the existing code: global flags before the subcommand, flags with values, and abbreviations. Second, name one shared function that both the policy rule and the new wrapper call. Third, include a test case for each form in the criterion's demonstration. Fourth, check these before the critic's first round with a mechanical check. That check should compare the forms the policy accepts with the forms the plan's tests cover. Separately, deviations from the deliverables list that a decision already explains should be passed to the critic as accepted, not raised again as findings. This is a change to the planning stage, not a default, because the check has to run in code before the critic does.
proposed_request: Take a build slot for each producer cargo command. When the producer runs `cargo` through Bash, the command must wait for and hold a Producer-class build slot (SlotQueue, Class::Producer) for as long as it runs. The slot must be taken whatever the invocation form: bare `cargo build`, `test`, `clippy` and `check`, and also with global flags before the subcommand (such as `cargo -q build` and `cargo --locked test`, per CARGO_GLOBAL_FLAGS in policy.rs). The policy rule that requires the wrapper and the wrapper itself must find the subcommand with one shared function, so they cannot disagree. Acceptance criteria: (1) Tests run each of `cargo build`, `cargo -q build`, `cargo --locked test`, `cargo clippy` and `cargo check` through the wrapper and show that each one holds a slot while it runs; (2) a command that is not a cargo build command takes no slot; (3) a recorded slotted command does not fail the invocation, and the record shows the build_slots count and the peak, sampled whenever a producer command runs, and the test fails when the feature is removed; (4) the hook's PATH check is stated, with a test showing what happens when the PATH differs from the Bash tool's. The following files are allowed deliverables because each is the only place that can do the job or needs a one-line edit to compile: crates/athena-core/src/invocation.rs, crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs, crates/athena-core/src/pr_check.rs, crates/athena-gate/src/reconcile.rs, crates/athena-gate/src/landing_tests.rs and docs/records.md. Do not raise these as scope findings.
